code: cmsHANDLE  CMSEXPORT cmsIT8LoadFromMem(cmsContext ContextID, const void *Ptr, cmsUInt32Number len)
note: Attacker-controlled raw CGATS/IT8 bytes (an ill-formed file whose quoted string is never terminated before end of input) enter the parser here.
Input bytes are copied into MemoryBlock; a NUL terminator is appended so that at the end of input NextCh() yields it8->ch == 0 forever.
Character feeder for the in-memory stream: once Source reaches the trailing NUL of MemoryBlock, it8->ch becomes 0 and stops advancing, so every subsequent call yields the same EOF character.
The stray opening quote of the unterminated string is tokenized; the parser dispatches to InStringSymbol() to read the quoted string.

Root cause: the string-reading loop only terminates on the closing quote, '\n' or '\r'. At end of input it8->ch == 0, which matches none of them, so the loop never terminates for an unterminated string.
The non-terminating loop keeps appending the EOF character (NUL) to the dynamic string, growing s->len without any input-driven bound.

Sink: when the string must grow, s->max *= 10 eventually overflows cmsInt32Number; AllocChunk() then returns a small (or NULL) buffer and memcpy() copies the huge s->len bytes into it, producing a heap buffer overflow / invalid write that aborts the process.
